newsitem.title: QATAR: GCC ministers to discuss Qatar-Bahrain row in Cairo.
newsitem.headline: GCC ministers to discuss Qatar-Bahrain row in Cairo.

text.p: Foreign ministers of the six Arab Gulf nations due to attend a Damascus Declaration meeting in Cairo on Saturday will discuss a border dispute between Qatar and Bahrain, a senior Qatari official said on Wednesday.
"The meeting will be held within the framework of the recent decision by the Doha summit," the official told Reuters.
A Gulf Corporation Council (GCC) summit in the Qatari capital Doha this month, which was boycotted by Manama, decided to set up a committee to resolve the rift between the two Gulf neighbours.
Bahrain and Qatar have been locked in a decades-old dispute over a cluster of small islands and sandbanks in the Gulf controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s but also claimed by Qatar.
Qatar has taken the case to the International Court of Justice in The Hague. The move has angered Bahrain, which prefers a regional solution.
Tension culminated between the two states when Bahrain accused a Qatari man and woman of spying and sentenced them on Wednesday to three years in prison each.
Qatar had accused Manama earlier of supporting an anti-government plot, which Doha said it had foiled in February.
"The meeting (in Cairo) will try to narrow the differences between the two neighbours and stop the open war of words currently raging between them", the official said.

It was not immediately clear why the GCC foreign ministers' meeting will be held on the sidelines of the Damascus Declaration meeting, but the Qatari official said Egypt, a member of the eight-state alliance, had appealed to Qatar and Bahrain to settle their differences within the Arab countries' framework.

Egypt, Syria and the six GCC members Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain and Oman formed their Damascus Delaration alliance after they united under the U.S.-led 1991 offensive that drove Iraqi forces out of Kuwait.
